title: Follow SLi-Rec parameter placement after native device moves
head: 4d1b220158d15d93636e565f2298560fe0cb484c
body:
### Description

SLi-Rec stores the device selected at construction in a plain attribute. Native module migration moves parameters but leaves that attribute unchanged, so dataset tensors, regularization and checkpoint loading can use a different device from the model.

Read the device from the item-embedding weights instead. Initial automatic CPU/CUDA selection is preserved; native `to()`, `cpu()` and `to_empty()` then require no separate metadata update. Parameter names and checkpoint tensors remain unchanged.

Fixes #2470.

### Validation

[Independent validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/recommenders/actions/runs/43907660754) checks exact head `4d1b220158d15d93636e565f2298560fe0cb484c` on Python 3.10/PyTorch 2.0.1 and Python 3.11/PyTorch 2.5.1:

- Unchanged model suite: **12 passed** in both environments.
- New cases on unchanged staging: **4 failed, 1 passing control, 2 CUDA-only skips**.
- Patched full model suite: **17 passed, 2 CUDA-only skips** in both environments.
- Native meta transitions reproduce the original full-forward mixed-device failure and verify batch placement, shapes, dtypes and regularization. Meta cases assess placement rather than numerical predictions.
- A native CPU → meta → CPU round trip restores an actual checkpoint, reproduces every saved prediction exactly and runs finite-gradient SGD steps that change parameters. No mocked device operators are used.
- CUDA-to-CPU tests cover both `cpu()` and `to("cpu")`, including checkpoint loading, prediction and training. They are committed but skipped on these CPU runners; no CUDA execution is claimed.
- Black and `git diff --check` pass. Local Python 3.12.14/PyTorch 2.5.1 gives the same results.

The validation also combines this change with the exact updated attention fix in #2453. Its CPU test no longer assigns device metadata. Combined results are **31 passed, 2 CUDA-only skips** on PyTorch 2.5.1 and **27 passed, 6 skips** on 2.0.1 (two CUDA cases plus four independently confirmed unsupported CPU-half cases).

### History review

Checked 1,497 pre-existing upstream PR heads and 69 fork branches, including all four reachable PyTorch sequential-base source versions from nine commits under current and former filenames. They all retain the initialization-time device. Earlier LightGCN graph-buffer work addresses unregistered graph tensors, a separate cause.

### Checklist

- [x] Contribution guidelines and code style followed.
- [x] Regressions added to the existing registered model test module.
- [x] Device property documents its native-migration behavior.
- [x] Commit includes the required `Signed-off-by` trailer.
- [x] Targets `staging`.
